intended_object: The standard 2×2 grid diagram of the unknot: O markings on the diagonal squares (0,0),(1,1) and X markings on the anti-diagonal squares (0,1),(1,0). This comes from the docstring and module documentation, following Ozsváth–Stipsicz–Szabó.
explanation: In this library, a `GridDiagram n` is a pair of permutation-graph states O and X with no column sharing an O and an X. That is the standard definition of a grid diagram, with one O and one X in every row and every column, in different squares. Here O is the identity state, which sends column 0 to row 0 and column 1 to row 1. X is the transposition state, which sends column 0 to row 1 and column 1 to row 0. These are exactly the two possible 2×2 permutation markings, and they are disjoint, so this is the unique (up to swapping the roles of O and X) 2×2 grid diagram. It represents the unknot. The library also proves `unknot_zero`, which identifies it with the n = 0 member of the general unknot family. It is a specific object, so the question of generality does not arise. The directions of `equivPerm` do not matter here, because both the identity and the swap are their own inverses.
